problem: score_area_for_finding (src/output/json/helpers.rs) bucketed a finding into "Landmarks / page structure" via `key.contains("navigation")` matched against the finding's full classification key, which included `finding.subcategory`. The shared `Subcategory::NavigationInteraction` label ("Navigation & Operation") covers ~26 unrelated WCAG rules (keyboard focus, timing, click target size, pointer gestures, drag operations, ...), so any of them fell through to "Landmarks / page structure" with a fabricated "main driver" whenever nothing earlier in the if/else chain matched first.
evidence: Confirmed live in 2 of 5 same-day single-report JSONs generated 2026-08-31: sauerstoffzentrum-nordost.de and shop.satower-mosterei.de both showed summary.accessibility_score_breakdown[] area="Landmarks / page structure" with main_driver="Insufficient click target size (N occurrences)" (rule a11y.target_size_minimum.small, WCAG 2.5.8) — a click-target-size finding has nothing to do with page landmarks.
expected: The "navigation" keyword should only match against a finding's own rule_id/title/description, never against the shared subcategory label, since that label is not specific to any one of the 8 report areas. "landmark" and "main" don't have this problem (no subcategory label contains either word) and can stay matched against the full key.
counter_examples: a11y.bypass_blocks.missing (title "Missing bypass navigation") must still classify into "Landmarks / page structure" — the match comes from its own title, not merely the shared subcategory label; see score_area_for_finding_still_classifies_bypass_navigation_as_landmarks.
a11y.landmark_main.missing (rule_id contains "landmark") must still classify into "Landmarks / page structure"; see score_area_for_finding_still_classifies_landmark_main_as_landmarks.
